# Independent audit: equal-depth facet flux and global critical circuits

Audited `candidate f2d1fbdd5a877f5b` in full,
including its exact critical-cover dependency. Result: PASS for the
stated results. `supporting computation verify_equal_depth_facet_flux.py` was rerun and passes.

One requested scope clarification has been applied by the root:
Section 4's base-affine shear now explicitly retains p_0!=p_1. This
was already inherited from Section 1's base-distinct setup. The valid same-base
extension in Sections 2.1 and 3 does not permit a base-affine shear to
identify distinct continuous endpoints in one fiber. The circuit
extraction itself does not need this shear, but its displayed formula
does need distinct bases.

## 1. Attainment, interiors, and the common equality cap

The anchored compactification is valid. Finite limiting evaluations
of the integer coefficients determine a convergent functional on their
span. Subtracting its convergent projection and adding its limit makes
those evaluations exact, while changing the divergent evaluations by
quantities tending to zero. One finite, sufficiently late coefficient
therefore realizes all full/empty divergent traces with the limiting
unit continuous normal. Finite thresholds converge in mass because
their within-fiber hyperplanes have zero d-volume. The anchor equation
is preserved throughout.

A vertical containing cap cannot lower the infimum: nonvertical tilts
retain its strict-sign fibers and capture at most its full boundary
fibers. Closed boundary mass is handled in the correct direction.

Positive depth in a positive fiber implies relative interior in that
fiber, by the supporting-height affine-majorant argument. The cited
critical-cover note separately handles zero-volume fibers by restricting
to their minimal base face; none is silently treated as a positive
section source here. Minkowski interpolation of interior balls makes
an intermediate mixed-integer point interior in its own positive fiber.

For a hypothetical equal-depth cap, a positive endpoint margin permits
a parallel shift removing a strictly positive slab from that endpoint's
own fiber. The other endpoint signs then force both margins to be
zero. Thus the SAME cap is actually minimizing at both endpoints, and
their depths both equal the intermediate depth. This is stronger than
a merely formal section-centroid condition.

## 2. The base and ambient flux identities

For a base functional, the proper-section derivative has coefficient
h(z)-h(p_e), with the original continuous normal of norm one. At a
supporting section the two one-sided derivatives are zero and that
coefficient times its section measure. Interpolating the two derivatives
at a local minimum produces allowable endpoint weights; independent
choices of their components are never presumed. Subtracting the two
scalar stationarity equations gives exactly

    A=sum B_z[theta_z^1(h(z)-1)-theta_z^0 h(z)],

whose pointwise upper bound is the stated distance to [0,1]. The signs
and the full compulsory proper-section term A are correct.

For an ambient affine functional the rotating-plane calculation also
checks. In fixed original-normal coordinates the new threshold is

    t>=-epsilon(h_0-h(y_e))/(1+epsilon b).

The denominator contributes no first-order correction beyond the
displayed numerator. Proper sections give the integral of h_0-h(y_e).
On a supporting face on the t<=0 side, the right derivative is the
positive-part integral and the left derivative the negative-part
integral. On the t>=0 side those formulas interchange. These signs
are correct for both cap gain and loss. The local slab bound, convex
interpolation to the supporting face, and null relative boundaries
justify the limits even for arbitrary convex, nonpolyhedral fibers.
A zero-area face contributes o(|epsilon|). The d=1 endpoint rule is
the same calculation with H_0 section measure.

Consequently one measurable supporting trace per endpoint suffices.
No untracked within-fiber Jacobian, ambient section factor, or coordinate
component selection appears. The ambient version genuinely includes
distinct endpoints in the SAME fiber.

## 3. Structural consequences and the finite circuit

In the support-null subclass, the flux right side vanishes and A>0,
so strict interpolation follows for all distinct positive-depth
endpoints whose intermediate point is mixed-integer. This yields at
most one global maximizing point per integer parity class, including
same-base uniqueness. The hypothesis explicitly excludes positive-area
supporting facets and is not available in a full OC argument.

The antipodal-base-slab consequence is also exact: a base functional
in [0,1] on all positive bases makes every exterior-distance term zero.

At a global plateau, the cited finite critical-cover construction
provides at most 2^n(d+1) actual nonvertical closed caps of mass at most
beta M. Each cap containing the intermediate point has mass exactly
beta M and must have that point on its boundary; otherwise its own
fiber-interior slab permits a lower-mass parallel containing cut.
The equality argument then puts both endpoints on that boundary.

The finitely many other closed caps miss a neighborhood. The containing
caps cover a ball in the intermediate fiber, and their homogeneous
continuous restrictions therefore cover all of R^d. Separation and
minimal convex dependence give a strictly positive circuit of at most
d+1 normals, with rank one less than its size. Every member is an
ACTUAL critical cap satisfying the same endpoint flux inequality.
This does not require differentiability, a complete description of the
depth region, or an exchange of fiberwise maxima.

For distinct bases, the stated affine fiber translation has determinant
one, preserves every integer base and every fiber volume, and transforms
the integer coefficients so that a_i'.(p_1-p_0)=0. The common continuous
normals retain their positive balance. Positive-area supporting sections
of polytopal fibers are facets, so the resulting finite incidence
restriction is correctly stated.

The layered-cube calibration gives A=3^n and exterior charge 5^(n-1),
with the first feasible dimension n=4. The cited candidates are not
global maximizers. Neither this calibration nor the balanced circuit
excludes a global plateau for general faceted fibers, and the note
expressly leaves that case unproved.
